**Chapter V4 - Access Control** 

Here are a few things I observed reviewing this chapter for v.5.0 for sanity check related to #2582: 

_Question 1_: Why did we not have the term "principle of least privilege" in this chapter anymore? Isn't that OWASP 101 basic web security principle to have and teach people? 

_Question 2_: Why are we moving away from recommending administrators to use multi-factor authentication (MFA) as a basic principle? Has something changed?

comments.body:
> Question 1: Why did we not have the term "principle of least privilege" in this chapter anymore? Isn't that OWASP 101 basic web security principle to have and teach people?

https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2196

> Question 2: Why are we moving away from recommending administrators to use multi-factor authentication (MFA) as a basic principle? Has something changed?

Please point to the precise requirement and change that you are talking about.

I see that we no longer mention "principle of least privilege" anywhere in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x12-V4-Access-Control.md

May I suggest we add it to the introduction section? Perhaps change the intro from:

_Authorization is the process of allowing access only to permitted consumers (users, servers and other clients). Ensure that a verified application satisfies the following high-level requirements:_

: to : 

_Authorization ensures that access is granted only to permitted consumers (users, servers, and other clients). To enforce the Principle of Least Privilege (POLP), verified applications must meet the following requirements:_

... or similar so it's at least mentioned?

> Question 2: Why are we moving away from recommending administrators to use multi-factor authentication (MFA) as a basic principle? Has something changed?
> 
> Please point to the precise requirement and change that you are talking about.

Hi @elarlang, regarding this precise requirement, it's not anymore in our past Github repo files in ASVS v.4.0, but I only found it in the published [ASVS 4.0.2 PDF](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/releases/download/v4.0.2_release/OWASP.Application.Security.Verification.Standard.4.0.2-en.pdf)  in requirement `4.3.1 - Verify administrative interfaces use appropriate multi-factor authentication to prevent unauthorized use.` 

In our current ASVS 5.0 requirement for the same number states, `4.3.1 [MODIFIED, LEVEL L1 > L3] Verify that access to administrative interfaces incorporates multiple layers of security, including continuous consumer identity verification, device security posture assessment, and contextual risk analysis, ensuring that network location or trusted endpoints are not the sole factors for authorization even though they may reduce the likelihood of unauthorized access.` which does not anymore mention multi-factor authentication (MFA). While "multiple layers of security" covers it, I still think it is reasonable and good information to mention MFA at least in the introduction section as what @jmanico proposes. :)

I would like to track question 1 in #2196 as it appears that some wording was discussed there but never adopted.

For question 2, @csfreak92 please can you read through #1086 to see if it answers your question. In general, we are mandating MFA for all from L2.

I can also see the benefit of adding MFA to 4.3.1.

I am certain Elar and Josh have more insight than I do here, I’d go with his suggestion.

We added POLP principle back in and it's committed and in master. https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2196 is closed out. 

If we do not want to add MFA to 4.3.1 can we close this out?
I will close this but @csfreak92 if you still have questions on 4.3.1, please refer to #1086 and tag me there if necessary

Yup, read through the long threads. Will concede that MFA is being addressed on other requirements such as 2.2.9. I just thought it was nice to still drill the idea that admin interfaces should have MFA strictly enforced vs normal users that's why I have it mentioned in the V4 sanity check issue above.
